title: Abusive text transformation using LLMs
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the effectiveness of LLMs in transforming abusive and toxic text (including religious hate speech) into non-abusive language while attempting to preserve the original semantic intent. It specifically analyzed the presence of offensive n-grams targeting religious groups before and after transformation, and measured the sentiment distribution and semantic similarity of the transformed texts compared to the original inputs.
findings: All models successfully reduced abusive language targeting religious groups. DeepSeek-V3 and GPT-4o tended to preserve much of the original context (e.g., maintaining n-grams like 'sharia law' or 'profit muhammad') while neutralizing the abuse, resulting in higher semantic similarity to the original text. In contrast, Groq and Gemini leaned heavily toward rewriting the text into a highly positive and collaborative tone, which frequently resulted in omitting the religious references and significantly altering the original semantic meaning.
